Use case: identity-preserve / precise-object-edit.
Asset type: 2D game sprite accessory worn by Impactus.
Edit the FIRST reference image: the full original white-and-purple robot sprite. Keep the robot's exact pose, face, expression, helmet volume, ears, hands, body proportions, purple armor, cape and pixel registration unchanged. The second reference is ONLY an example of convincing WORN fit, not the outfit to copy. The third reference is the old hat style to improve.
Change ONLY the headwear. Draw a warm cognac explorer fedora, with a soft dented crown, dark brown woven band, small antique brass buckle and neatly stitched short curved brim. It must genuinely wrap around this robot's rounded helmet in its same three-quarter view: the crown contains the top of the helmet, the back brim goes behind the helmet and the front brim crosses its upper forehead. A close soft contact shadow follows the forehead curvature. Keep the black face, cyan eyes, and purple ear discs fully unobscured. Conceal the helmet crest only where the hat naturally covers it. This is a 2D raster illustration matching the source shading, NOT a new 3D character model. Do not float a product photograph above the head.
Composition: one complete original robot in precisely the same position and scale inside a square canvas as image 1, all feet and hat inside canvas. Make the hat compact enough to fit the existing upper margin; no shrinking robot to make space. No extra accessories, no backpack, no text, no border, no layout. Output true RGBA transparent background, never paint a checkerboard. Light comes from the upper left. Crisp premium game illustration.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: independent REAR CAPE layer for an existing 2D game character, composited behind the unchanged original robot.
Reference image: the original Impactus sprite, ONLY for the exact worn viewpoint, cape drape, folded silhouette, lighting and visual style. Do not include any part of the robot in the output.
Primary request: Paint a complete cape that fits behind this robot in precisely this three-quarter front view. The two shoulders are close together near the upper center, the fabric falls and flares to the left and more broadly to the right. The left side is narrower, the right lobe is wide. Keep the natural curved folded lower hem and broad soft folds of the reference cape. Fill in all cloth that the robot normally hides: one continuous opaque cloth, no arm-shaped gaps or ghost body parts. This is a soft wearable fabric cloak, NOT stiff wings, a flat rectangle, a costume on a mannequin or a cape viewed from the rear.
Design: Signature Impactus city-guardian cape. Royal violet and deep purple satin, warm ivory-gold piping; a restrained embroidered skyline of a green city runs along the wide lower RIGHT edge, with three simple houses, a tree and a flowing path. One small elegant ivory lightning-and-leaf insignia above the skyline. Purple lining, tailored panel seams. Keep the original purple identity.
Draw ornaments woven/embroidered into the curved fabric and following the folds, with convincing fabric shading, subtle texture, tangible hem trim. Elegant bold shapes legible at a small game sprite size; avoid a busy collage or tiny scattered symbols.
Framing: cloak only, no robot, no head, no hands, no body, no straps floating outside the cloak, no hanger. Spread silhouette approximately twice as wide as high, upper neck at center slightly left; keep whole cloak within frame with clear transparent margin. Light from upper left, same polished illustrated game art as reference. No text, no watermark, no floor shadow. Output true transparent RGBA background, do not draw any checkerboard.
